title: Device Clock Wrong During Enrollment — Jump or Sustained Offset
description: The device's clock changed by five or more minutes mid-session (clock jump) or ran five or more minutes off server time for the whole session (sustained offset), measured against the server receive frame of every uploaded event. Complements ANALYZE-DEV-007, which is a one-shot NTP check at agent startup and misses devices where NTP was unreachable or the clock changed later. IME-log-derived events are excluded from the measurement.
author: Autopilot Monitor
explanation:
This device's {{skewSummary}} (five-minute threshold). A clock that is off by five or more minutes breaks time-sensitive enrollment mechanisms: Kerberos tolerates at most 5 minutes of skew (Hybrid Join), Entra ID token validation allows about 5 minutes on token lifetimes, and freshly issued SCEP/PKCS certificates can be rejected as "not yet valid" when the clock is more than ~10 minutes behind the CA.

Unlike ANALYZE-DEV-007 (a one-shot NTP comparison at agent startup), this finding is measured across the whole session against the server's receive time — it also catches devices where the NTP check could not run (UDP 123 blocked) or where the clock changed after startup (time sync correcting a wrong RTC, Windows auto-timezone, manual change).

remediation.title: Fix the device clock and time source
steps: Check the BIOS/RTC clock and the CMOS battery if the wrong time recurs on the same hardware.
At OOBE, run 'w32tm /resync /force' (Shift+F10 command prompt) to sync with time.windows.com.
Ensure UDP port 123 to time.windows.com is open in the deployment network.
Review 'Set time automatically' and 'Set time zone automatically' behavior on the deployment image — automatic timezone changes mid-enrollment show up as clock jumps.
